2CO.P.3.7-18.text: The Glory of the New Covenant

2CO.1.3-4.text: God comforts Paul so he can comfort others

2CO.1.5-7.text: Paul’s sufferings and comfort help the Corinthians

2CO.1.8-10.text: Paul almost died in Asia and trusted God

2CO.1.11-11.text: The Corinthians’ prayers help Paul and bring thanks to God

2CO.1.12-14.text: Paul boasts that he acted with holiness and sincerity

2CO.1.15-16.text: Paul planned to visit the Corinthians twice

2CO.1.17-18.text: Paul did not change his plans carelessly

2CO.1.19-20.text: All God’s promises are made certain in Christ

2CO.1.21-22.text: God makes Paul and the Corinthians firm in Christ

2CO.1.23-24.text: Paul did not return to Corinth to spare the believers

2CO.2.1-2.text: Paul decides not to make another painful visit

2CO.2.3-4.text: Paul wrote in tears to show his love for the church

2CO.2.5-7.text: Paul urges the church to forgive and comfort the man

2CO.2.8-9.text: Paul asks the church to show love to the man again

2CO.2.10-11.text: Paul forgives the man so Satan cannot outwit believers

2CO.2.12-13.text: Paul has no peace in Troas and goes to Macedonia

2CO.2.14-15.text: Paul thanks God for spreading the knowledge of Christ

2CO.2.16-17.text: Paul speaks sincerely as a man sent from God

2CO.3.1-3.text: The Corinthians are Christ’s letter written on hearts

2CO.3.4-6.text: God makes Paul able to serve the new covenant

2CO.3.7-8.text: The ministry of the Spirit has even more glory

2CO.3.9-11.text: The glory that lasts is greater than the fading glory

2CO.3.12-13.text: Paul is bold, unlike Moses who covered his face

2CO.3.14-16.text: The veil is taken away when anyone turns to the Lord

2CO.3.17-18.text: The Spirit brings freedom and changes believers

2CO.4.1-2.text: Paul does not lose heart and speaks the truth openly

2CO.4.3-4.text: The god of this age blinds unbelievers to the gospel

2CO.4.5-6.text: Paul preaches Christ as Lord, not himself

2CO.4.7-10.text: Paul is pressed on all sides but not destroyed

2CO.4.11-12.text: Paul faces death so that life works in the Corinthians

2CO.4.13-15.text: Paul speaks in faith, knowing God will raise believers

2CO.4.16-18.text: Paul does not lose heart but looks at what is unseen

2CO.5.1-3.text: Believers will have an eternal house from God in heaven

2CO.5.4-5.text: God has given believers the Spirit as a promise

2CO.5.6-8.text: Paul prefers to be at home with the Lord

2CO.5.9-10.text: Paul wants to please God; all must face Christ’s judgment

2CO.5.11-12.text: Paul hopes the Corinthians see that he is sincere

2CO.5.13-15.text: Christ’s love compels Paul because Christ died for all

2CO.5.16-17.text: Paul says anyone in Christ is a new creation

2CO.5.18-19.text: God gave Paul the message of reconciliation

2CO.5.20-21.text: Paul urges the Corinthians to be reconciled to God

2CO.6.1-3.text: Paul urges the Corinthians not to receive grace in vain

2CO.6.4-7.text: Paul commends himself as God’s servant in hardships

2CO.6.8-10.text: Paul has nothing, yet possesses everything

2CO.6.11-13.text: Paul asks the Corinthians to welcome him openly

2CO.6.14-16.text: Believers must not be partners with unbelievers

2CO.6.17-18.text: God calls believers to be separate and be his children

2CO.7.1-1.text: Paul urges believers to make themselves clean and holy

2CO.7.2-4.text: Paul has wronged no one and is proud of the Corinthians

2CO.7.5-7.text: God comforted Paul through the arrival of Titus

2CO.7.8-10.text: Paul’s letter caused sorrow that led to repentance

2CO.7.11-12.text: Godly sorrow made the Corinthians eager to do right

2CO.7.13-14.text: Titus was refreshed and Paul’s boasting proved true

2CO.7.15-16.text: Paul rejoices that he can trust the Corinthians fully

2CO.8.1-2.text: The churches of Macedonia gave generously in poverty

2CO.8.3-5.text: The Macedonians gave freely and gave themselves to the Lord

2CO.8.6-7.text: Paul urges the Corinthians to excel in giving

2CO.8.8-9.text: Paul points the Corinthians to Christ who became poor

2CO.8.10-12.text: Paul urges the Corinthians to finish their gift

2CO.8.13-15.text: Paul wants equality between the Corinthians and others

2CO.8.16-17.text: Paul thanks God for Titus’s eagerness to help

2CO.8.18-19.text: Paul sends a brother chosen by the churches with Titus

2CO.8.20-21.text: Paul wants to do right in handling the gift

2CO.8.22-24.text: Paul asks the Corinthians to show love to the messengers

2CO.9.1-2.text: Paul has boasted about the Corinthians’ eagerness to give

2CO.9.3-5.text: Paul sends the brothers so the gift is ready

2CO.9.6-7.text: Each believer should give gladly, not by force

2CO.9.8-9.text: God can give believers all they need to do good

2CO.9.10-11.text: God will increase what believers have so they can give

2CO.9.12-15.text: The gift brings thanks to God and help to believers

2CO.10.1-2.text: Paul appeals to the Corinthians to be gentle with him

2CO.10.3-4.text: Paul says his weapons are not those of the world

2CO.10.5-6.text: Paul will punish disobedience when the Corinthians obey

2CO.10.7-8.text: Paul says he belongs to Christ and has authority

2CO.10.9-10.text: Paul answers those who say his letters are strong

2CO.10.11-12.text: Paul will act as strongly as his letters say

2CO.10.13-14.text: Paul boasts only within the field God gave him

2CO.10.15-16.text: Paul hopes to preach the gospel beyond Corinth

2CO.10.17-18.text: Believers should boast only in the Lord

2CO.11.1-2.text: Paul is jealous for the Corinthians with godly jealousy

2CO.11.3-4.text: Paul fears the Corinthians will be led away from Christ

2CO.11.5-6.text: Paul says he is not inferior to the super-apostles

2CO.11.7-9.text: Paul preached to the Corinthians free of charge

2CO.11.10-11.text: Paul will keep boasting because he loves the Corinthians

2CO.11.12-13.text: Paul calls the false apostles deceitful workers

2CO.11.14-15.text: Satan and his servants pretend to be good

2CO.11.16-18.text: Paul asks the Corinthians to accept him as a fool

2CO.11.19-21.text: The Corinthians tolerate fools and harsh treatment

2CO.11.22-23.text: Paul is a Hebrew and a greater servant of Christ

2CO.11.24-26.text: Paul lists beatings and many dangers he suffered

2CO.11.27-29.text: Paul suffers hardship and cares for all the churches

2CO.11.30-31.text: Paul will boast only in his weakness

2CO.11.32-33.text: Paul escapes from Damascus in a basket

2CO.12.1-2.text: Paul tells of a man taken up to the third heaven

2CO.12.3-4.text: The man hears things in Paradise too sacred to tell

2CO.12.5-5.text: Paul will boast only about his weaknesses

2CO.12.6-7.text: God gives Paul a thorn to keep him humble

2CO.12.8-10.text: The Lord’s grace is enough for Paul in weakness

2CO.12.11-13.text: Paul says the Corinthians should have praised him

2CO.12.14-15.text: Paul will gladly spend himself for the Corinthians

2CO.12.16-18.text: Paul and Titus did not take advantage of the Corinthians

2CO.12.19-19.text: Paul says all he writes builds up the believers

2CO.12.20-21.text: Paul fears finding sin among the Corinthians

2CO.13.1-2.text: Paul warns the Corinthians he will not spare sinners

2CO.13.3-4.text: Christ is powerful among the Corinthians, not weak

2CO.13.5-6.text: Paul tells the Corinthians to test themselves

2CO.13.7-8.text: Paul prays that the Corinthians will do right

2CO.13.9-10.text: Paul writes to build up the church, not to tear down

2CO.13.11-12.text: Paul urges believers to live in peace and harmony

2CO.13.13-14.text: Paul ends with greetings and a prayer for grace
